claims.text: The applicable alloy is equimolar CoCrFeNiTi, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can exist as a simple solid-solution FCC state.
The proposed starting state has a low initial dislocation density.
Low hardness and strength in the stated alloy are primarily governed by low lattice friction and facile dislocation mobility.
Facile dislocation mobility produces rapid dynamic recovery during deformation.
Dynamic recovery limits the accumulation of dislocations.
The FCC state has a low Peierls barrier that facilitates rapid dislocation glide.
Dislocation annihilation and rearrangement into low-angle boundaries remove mobile or stored dislocations as deformation proceeds.
Restricted dislocation storage limits work hardening and thereby sustains low hardness and strength.
Only modest increases in dislocation density should occur during tensile deformation, including at higher strains.
Dynamic recovery should be observable in real time as dislocation annihilation and formation of low-angle boundaries.
Introducing minor precipitates would retard recovery.
Retarding recovery with minor precipitates would increase dislocation storage and strength.
The proposed mechanism is applicable at room temperature under tensile strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-1 s^-1 when grain size and texture are controlled.
Grain-boundary behavior and texture evolution may interact with the proposed dislocation dynamics.
TEM specimen-size effects may prevent in situ observations from fully representing bulk recovery behavior.
